newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA IN CONVINCING WIN OVER ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA IN CONVINCING WIN OVER ZIMBABWE.

text.p: COLOMBO, September 14 - Sri Lanka spinners Muthiah Muralitharan and Jayantha Silva took nine wickets between them to send Zimbabwe tumbling to defeat by an innings and 77 runs on the fourth day of the first test on Saturday.

Zimbabwe, trailing on the first innings by 204 runs, were bowled out for 127, their lowest total in test cricket, an hour after tea to give Sri Lanka their eight test victory, and the first by an innings.
Zimbabwe's previous lowest total was 134 against Pakistan at Karachi in 1993-4.

Off-spinner Muralitharan finished with a career best five for 33 off 20.3 overs, the sixth time he has taken five or more wickets in a test innings. Left-arm spinner Silva finished with four for 25 from 19 overs, also a personal test best.
The Zimbabwe innings was swiftly ended after tea with the last six wickets crashing for 14 runs in 66 minutes.
Muralitharan and Silva made full use of a turning pitch and were well supported in the field by Roshan Mahanama who snapped up four catches at slip.
Top scorer for Zimbabwe was Grant Flower with 27 before he became Muralitharan's first victim.

Captain Alistair Campbell batted for 133 minutes for 26 runs without once reaching the boundary and then also succumbed to Muralitharan. The only other resistance was from Guy Whittall who stayed 83 minutes for 13.
Play began after an early lunch after the morning session was washed out by rain.
The second and final test begins in Colombo on September 18.
